hypothesis: Stage A of the semantic decomposition (registry by index, goals with a closed kind, a type per goal, slot questions; chain, check, batch, choose, breakeven) formalizes numeric book problems better than the classic value and formula questions, on tiny and on good answering the same questions.

arms.A: decomposition on tiny (LocalLLMStepByStep B, product ladder tiny -> small -> good per question)
arms.C: classic problem questions on tiny (CHATSOP_PROBLEM_PROTOCOL=classic, control)

sample: stage 1: 10 fresh problems per book with at least two numbers in the question, books commonsense, decompose, adult, world, math (50); never a regression case or a seen item (tools/eval/formalization-regression/sample-stage.mjs, seed sd-stage1). Deviation from the design: stratified by book instead of by type, because the type strata need a labelling pass; the decomposition's own type choice is reported per problem.
metrics: correct / wrong / unknown / invalid / failed per arm and book; paired difference A - C with a paired bootstrap interval (10000 resamples); questions per problem; escalations; types chosen.
stopping: stage 1 only, then fix generically; stage 2 (25 per stratum) once, if stage 1 is undecided. Stop when the paired interval of A - C excludes 0 in either direction, or when more than 20% of A's turns fail (infrastructure).
gate: a change enters the product only with zero losses on the regression set (tools/eval/formalization-regression/gate.mjs, offline floor).
